pr_comments:
This adds a special helper inside `vo_gpu_next` to map properties of the `mp_image` directly. It is not strictly speaking what was requested in #8206, since that was asking for the ability to map *arbitrary* mpv parameters. That seems much harder to do, however.

Maybe this design is not the best, and it would be better to instead handle this at the mpv options layer, by transparently forwarding mpv properties to the shader opts dictionary.

I'm not really happy with this approach, to be honest.

Not sure if I should comment here, please excuse me if not.

I'm looking at rendering spherical videos using un360 (https://gist.github.com/tesu/196db5421559de3e9555d4f9da9d847d). There are everything in there, except navigation in the sphere.  
The approach I feel would fit, and fits this PR, is to be able to use newly created variables : we use input.conf to define values when keys are pressed (like KP_8 for up), and modify named variable (`pitch = pitch + 0.1`). Then, the glsl is hooked to those same names, and use them dynamically.

Another approach would be to call functions of the glsl when we press a key, but that doesn't fit this PR ;)

issue_context.title: [gpu_next] mpv properties (ex: time) as a shader parameter (was transition shaders)
issue_context.body:
### Expected behavior of the wanted feature
The following example shader displays an orange bloc that moves on screen at mpv first launch (based on frame): 
https://github.com/butterw/bShaders/blob/master/mpv/cs_wkgroups.hook.glsl

**I would like to be able to trigger transition shaders, at each new file played (in a playlist for instance). This would be possible if play time in seconds was available as a parameter to shaders.**  

**Feature request: expand available uniform parameters available to user shaders:**
1) Make time in seconds available as a uniform float parameter to user shaders (like mpc-hc/be). This enables timed effects (independantly of the frame rate which could be 25, 30 or 60fps, etc.). 
It can also be used as a seed for PRNG. The glsl version of this noise shader produces an undesirable pattern using frame or random: https://github.com/butterw/bShaders/blob/master/FilmGrain_Noise/bNoise.hlsl

2) Make play time in seconds (or play frame ?), which resets to zero at each new file available to user shaders. The value 0 could be used to trigger a transition effect.
comments:
For transition effects specifically, it might be simpler to introduce a !WHEN condition on playtime to enable/disable the shader in the pass header: 
The shader is enabled WHEN a new input file is loaded and for a specified duration. 
   
A time uniform (1.) would still would be useful in shaders: 
- "random" is a fixed sequence ? unless you can change the seed of the PRNG it isn't actually random at all.
- being able to have random effects would be desirable. 
- the logic required for handling timed effects (start, stop, repetition, duration) isn't that simple, as demonstrated by this example shader for mpc-hc: 
https://github.com/butterw/bShaders/blob/master/bStrobe.hlsl

As mentionned in #9967 it is now possible to pass a float (or int) value to a vo_gpu_next shader. 

AFAIK what is still missing is the ability to associate a mpv property (such as playback-time) to a shader, so that the shader parameter is continuously updated.

> AFAIK what is still missing is the ability to associate a mpv property (such as playback-time) to a shader

Try this.

![image](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/assets/50797982/57647e60-01c6-408f-8c6f-8361ff29ae5f)

```lua
mp.observe_property("playback-time", "native", function(_, v)
    -- print(v)
    mp.command("no-osd set glsl-shader-opts p=" .. v)
end)
```

review_comments: It is UB to assign values form outside the variable range. Should be clampled here, also consider using `lrintf` that would help.
